title: Safe use of kitchen equipment, knives, burns and scalds
siteNotes: Which machines (slicer, mixer, mincer and so on) the venue has, and which staff are authorised and trained to use each one
Where each machine's guard, isolator and emergency stop are, and how to lock it off before cleaning
The venue's knife storage (block, magnetic strip or drawer) and where cut-resistant gloves are kept, if used
How the fryers are filtered, drained and changed, and who is allowed to do it
Where the first aid kit, the nearest cold running water, and the first aiders are
How to report faulty equipment and how it is tagged or taken out of use
Where the wet floor signs and spill kit are kept
legalNotes: Equipment must be suitable, maintained, guarded and used by trained people: Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (PUWER), regs 4 to 9, 11 and 12. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1998/2306

Risk assessment and training: Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, regs 3 and 13; Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 ss. 2 and 7 (employees must take reasonable care and co-operate).

Isolating machines before cleaning and keeping guards in place: HSE catering guidance on slicers and mixers (https://www.hse.gov.uk/catering/). Stated in general terms; the venue's own machine instructions take priority. HSE pages were not re-fetched for this session.

Burns and scalds: cool the burn or scald under cool running water for 20 minutes; do not use creams, butter or sticky dressings; do not burst blisters or remove clothing stuck to the burn. Call 999 for a very large or deep burn, one on the face, genitals or bottom, or a chemical or electrical burn. Source: NHS https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds/. Verified.

Knife handling, fryer safety and wet-floor practice are common good practice drawn from HSE catering guidance; no specific figures are given. Slips and wet floors are covered in more depth in the Slips, trips and falls session.
Not verified: any minimum age rules for machinery (not mentioned in the session on purpose); any penalty figures.

Review 6 Oct 2026: burns advice re-checked against nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds (cool or lukewarm running water for 20 minutes, as soon as possible and within 3 hours; take off jewellery and clothing near the burn unless stuck; lay cling film over it, do not wrap it; no ice, creams, oils, butter or sticky dressings; do not burst blisters; 999 for very large or deep burns, face, genitals or bottom, and chemical, acid or electrical burns). Changes: added removal of jewellery and clothing near the burn (swelling), and replaced 'clean non-fluffy cloth' with the NHS cling film advice (lay it on, do not wrap it round). Note the NHS also lists burns bigger than the casualty's hand and burns on hands, feet, joints and neck as needing hospital (A&E) assessment; the session teaches 999 triggers only, and a small burn on the hand should still be reported to a manager and, if in doubt, checked by a first aider or NHS 111.

Nothing in the session states a legal minimum age or penalty for machinery use. Young workers (under 18) have extra protections under the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999 (reg. 19, protection of young persons); not taught here and not verified.

cards.title: Safe use of kitchen equipment, knives, burns and scalds
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- handle knives and machines safely
- work safely with hot oil and hot liquids
- give first aid for a burn and report faulty equipment

cards.title: Knives: carry, cut, clean, store
cards.body: A sharp, clean knife is safer than a blunt one. Never try to catch a falling knife. Your manager will show you where knives are stored.

items.title: Carry
items.text: Point down, close to your side, call 'behind'

items.title: Cut
items.text: On a stable board, fingers curled away

items.title: Clean
items.text: One at a time, blade away from you

items.title: Store
items.text: In the block or rack, never loose in the sink

cards.title: Guards on, power off
cards.body: Only trained staff use slicers and mixers. Keep the guards on and in place every time. Before cleaning, adjusting or clearing a jam, **switch off, unplug or isolate** and wait for the blade or bowl to stop. Tie hair back, roll up sleeves and take off loose jewellery, and never wear loose clothing near moving parts. Your manager will show you which machines you may use and how to isolate them.

cards.title: Fryers and hot oil
cards.body: Hot oil causes some of the worst burns. Do not overfill, and keep water and wet food out of hot oil. Lower food in slowly. Never move or filter hot oil unless you have been trained and the oil has cooled to the safe level shown in your instructions. Your manager will show you who changes the oil.

items.title: Keep water out
items.text: Dry food and wet baskets spit and splash

items.title: Lower slowly
items.text: Do not drop food in or overfill

items.title: Cool first
items.text: Never carry or filter hot oil without training

cards.title: Hot liquids and steam
cards.body: Scalds from hot water, stock, tea urns and steam are common. Use dry oven gloves, not wet cloths, and lift lids away from you so steam escapes safely. Carry pans only as far as you need to, with a clear path. Say 'hot' or 'behind' as you go. Fill a pot no more than the level you can carry safely.

cards.title: Burns and scalds: first aid
cards.body: Cool the burn under cool running water for **20 minutes**, as soon as possible. Take off jewellery and clothing near it, but do not pull off anything stuck to the burn. Do not use ice, creams or butter, and do not burst blisters. Call 999 if it is large or deep, on the face, genitals or bottom, or caused by chemicals or electricity. Tell a manager and record it. Your manager will show you the first aiders and the nearest running water.

items.title: Cool for 20 minutes
items.text: Cool running water, as soon as possible

items.title: Cover loosely
items.text: Lay cling film over it. Do not wrap it round

items.title: Call 999 if serious
items.text: Large, deep, face, chemical or electrical

cards.title: Wet floors and faulty kit
cards.body: Wipe up spills at once and put out a wet floor sign. If a machine looks damaged, a guard is missing or it behaves oddly, **do not use it**. Switch it off, stop others using it, and tell your manager. Your manager will show you how faults are reported and how kit is tagged out of use.

right.title: Do not
items: Carry on with a missing guard

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Carry knives point down, cut on a stable board, wash one at a time.
- Guards on, switch off and isolate before cleaning, no loose clothing.
- Keep water out of hot oil. Do not move hot oil.
- Burn or scald: cool running water for 20 minutes, then get help.
- Faulty or unguarded kit: do not use it, tell your manager.

cards.q: The slicer jams halfway through a ham. What is the right thing to do?
options: Poke the meat clear with a utensil while running
Slow the machine down and lift the guard
Switch off, isolate, wait for the blade, then clear it
Reach in quickly with a folded cloth
cards.why: A blade can be dangerous even when it seems to be stopping. Switch off and isolate before you reach near it.

cards.q: Putting butter on a fresh burn helps it heal.
cards.why: NHS advice is to cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes. Butter, creams and oils should not be used.

cards.q: How long should a small burn be held under cool running water?
options: About 2 minutes
About 5 minutes
About 10 minutes
20 minutes
cards.why: NHS advice is 20 minutes, as soon as possible. Shorter than that does not cool the skin enough.

cards.q: Which TWO are safe practice with a deep fat fryer?
options: Lower food in slowly
Drop a wet basket straight in to save time
Keep water out of the oil
Move hot oil to the sink yourself
Overfill it to save changing the oil
cards.why: Slow lowering and keeping water out stop splashes and spitting. Hot oil should not be moved by untrained staff.

cards.q: The mixer's guard is missing and a colleague says it is fine for one batch. What do you do?
options: Use it carefully, just for this one batch
Use it on the lowest speed setting only
Tell the chef it still works fine
Do not use it; tell your manager
cards.why: Equipment must have its guards. A missing guard means it should not be used until it is fixed.

cards.q: You drop a knife while carrying it across a busy kitchen. What do you do?
options: Try to catch it before it lands
Grab it quickly by the blade
Step back and let it fall
Kick it under the nearest bench
cards.why: Never try to catch a falling knife. Step back, let it fall, then pick it up and check nobody is hurt.

cards.q: If you see a spill, you can leave it for the cleaner at the end of service.
cards.why: Wipe up spills at once and put out a wet floor sign. A wet floor is a slip hazard in minutes.

cards.q: A basket of frozen chips is wet with ice. How do you put it into hot oil?
options: Shake off ice, lower slowly
Drop it in fast and step back
Tip it in from a height
Add a splash of water to cool the oil
cards.why: Water and hot oil spit and splash violently. Shake off the ice and lower the basket slowly.

cards.q: You are carrying a pot of stock across the kitchen. What helps most?
options: Hurry, so it is not held for long
Carry it high to see over it
Use a damp cloth on the handles
Say 'hot, behind' with a clear path
cards.why: A clear path and a warning to colleagues prevent most scalds. Damp cloths conduct heat and steam.

cards.q: Which TWO mean you should call 999 for a burn?
options: It is small and on the hand
It is deep or very large
It is on the face
It is red and sore
It has a small blister
cards.why: NHS advice is to call 999 for a burn that is very large or deep, or on the face, genitals or bottom, or caused by chemicals or electricity.
